title: How to Talk Like a VIP
coreMove: Trim your self-presentation and everyday phrasing until every sentence carries useful information without begging for approval.
sourcePressure: Verbal-status unit covering techniques 24 through 37: identity-question answers, compressed self-description, stronger words, avoiding quick imitation, cliches, teasing, overeager gratitude, and keeping attention on the receiver.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The weak version is to sound fancy. The useful version is disciplined wording: precise, brief, receiver-aware, and free of cliches or needy embellishment.

counterintuition: Big words make you sound small
Do not joke with important people
tryThisNow: Remove filler words for one day
Use stronger verbs in your next email
examples: job interview tell me about yourself

exampleSpecs.domain: a wildlife rehabilitator answering what do you do at a county permit hearing
exampleSpecs.audience: a skilled practitioner whose rambling answer makes officials miss the public value
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether a temporary permit is renewed before spring intake season
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she crosses out three apologetic sentences on her note card and replaces them with one concrete line about returning injured hawks to the county fields
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a permit hearing note card with three lines struck through

exampleSpecs.domain: a bicycle framebuilder describing his craft to a hotel concierge arranging a private tour
exampleSpecs.audience: a quiet artisan who undersells himself with technical clutter
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether visiting cyclists see the shop as worth an afternoon detour
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: when asked what makes the tour special, he stops listing alloys and gives one clean sentence about fitting steel to the rider body and roads
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a brazing torch cooling beside a row of unfinished fork crowns

exampleSpecs.domain: a forensic accountant explaining a fraud finding to a family court mediator
exampleSpecs.audience: a specialist tempted to sound impressive with jargon
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the mediator understands the pattern quickly enough to pause settlement pressure
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she swaps a jargon-heavy explanation for a plain comparison between reported sales and deposit slips, then stops before adding credentials
exampleSpecs.firstImage: two columns of highlighted deposit slips clipped under a binder tab

exampleSpecs.domain: a perfumer presenting a custom scent to a hotel amenities buyer
exampleSpecs.audience: a creative expert whose poetic cliches make the buyer distrust the pitch
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether a boutique hotel chooses her soap and lotion line for a full season
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she looks at the phrase unforgettable journey on her sample card, tears it off, and describes the scent through two exact notes the buyer can smell
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a blotter strip drying beside a tiny amber vial

exampleSpecs.domain: a ferry captain making a safety announcement to tourists on a foggy crossing
exampleSpecs.audience: a seasoned operator who must sound calm without sounding bored
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether passengers follow instructions during low visibility
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he replaces the habitual welcome aboard cliche with exact instructions tied to the foghorn and orange rail markers
exampleSpecs.firstImage: fog beads collecting on the orange rail marker near the gangway

exampleSpecs.domain: a ceramicist responding to a collector who asks why one cracked glaze costs more
exampleSpecs.audience: an artist who either overexplains process or hides behind mystique
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the collector understands value without feeling sold to
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: after losing one sale to a cloudy answer, she practices naming the exact kiln risk and stops before apologizing for the price
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a tea bowl with a silver repair line resting on black felt

skillTargets: compress a self-description without making it vague
replace cliches with concrete receiver-useful language
decide when restraint is stronger than extra gratitude or teasing

tryThisNowSpec: Rewrite one answer you give often, such as what do you do, into one sentence with a concrete result, no apology, and no decorative adjective.
